name: Gulfport
title: Investor Renovation Contractor in Gulfport, MS | Genstone
metaDescription: Gulfport, MS investor rehab: flood-zone scopes, wind-rated roofs, Formosan termite repair and post-Katrina code work, managed by one field manager.
intro: On the Mississippi Gulf Coast, the first question about any rehab is not the kitchen. It is the flood zone, the base flood elevation, and how the wind and flood rules adopted after Hurricane Katrina apply to the house you are buying. In Gulfport those answers can change from one side of a street to the other, and they shape the scope, the insurance premium and the resale more than finish choices do. Genstone Construction renovates houses in Gulfport and across Harrison County for flippers, BRRRR investors, rental owners, 2–4 unit buyers, FHA 203(k) borrowers and REO asset managers. We coordinate vetted, licensed local contractors, and a designated field manager runs the job from the first walk-through to final billing. It starts with a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review that checks repair costs, flood and wind exposure and your ARV before you commit. After that you get a line-item scope with a draw schedule, permits handled with the city, documentation you can follow remotely, and no upfront payment.
housingStock:
Gulfport's housing was rearranged by a single storm. Hurricane Katrina's surge in 2005 wiped out or gutted a large share of the houses closest to the water, especially south of the CSX railroad tracks that run parallel to the beach. What stands there now is a mix of older survivors, houses that were rebuilt or raised afterward, and new construction sitting on pilings or tall piers. Buying in that band means reading the elevation certificate before anything else.

North of the tracks and up toward Interstate 10, the city is mostly post-war and mid-century: modest frame cottages from the 1940s, brick and frame ranch houses from the 1950s through the 1970s on slab foundations, and pockets of older raised cottages in Downtown Gulfport, Soria City and Mississippi City. Handsboro, one of the oldest parts of the city, still has houses dating to the nineteenth century, with the wood framing, tall ceilings and pier foundations that come with them. Turkey Creek, a historic community founded by freed families after the Civil War, sits along low ground where drainage matters on every lot.

Orange Grove and North Gulfport, north of the interstate, carry the newer inventory: subdivisions from the 1970s through the 2000s and a wave of post-Katrina building as families moved inland. Those houses are simpler to renovate but still bring their own era's issues, including early builder-grade plumbing and HVAC nearing the end of its life.

For a rehab, the practical takeaway is that construction era matters less here than location relative to flood zones and the date of the last major rebuild. A 1960s ranch that was gutted and rebuilt after Katrina may have newer wiring and drywall than a 1990s house inland, while an unrenovated older cottage near the beach may face strict rules the moment you cross the substantial-improvement line.

commonIssues.title: Flood zone and substantial improvement limits
commonIssues.body: Many Gulfport properties sit in FEMA special flood hazard areas. When renovation cost on a house below base flood elevation reaches the substantial improvement threshold relative to the structure's value, the whole house has to be brought into flood compliance, which can mean raising it. That single rule can turn a reasonable flip into an expensive project. We check flood zone, elevation certificate and past permits during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review so the scope stays on the right side of that line or plans for it openly.

commonIssues.title: Wind exposure and roof condition
commonIssues.body: Coastal Harrison County is exposed to hurricanes and tropical storms nearly every season, and roofs carry the most risk. Older houses often lack hurricane straps or proper roof-to-wall connections, and many roofs were patched rather than replaced after past storms. Insurers on the coast look hard at roof age and construction. Replacing a roof to current wind requirements, with sealed decking and the right fastening, often pays back through insurability and resale more than any interior upgrade does.

commonIssues.title: Formosan termites
commonIssues.body: The Gulf Coast has well-established Formosan termite populations, which build large colonies and can do serious structural damage faster than native subterranean termites. They nest above ground in wet wood as well as in soil, so roof leaks and plumbing leaks create new targets. Older raised cottages in Handsboro, Soria City and Downtown Gulfport are especially exposed. We recommend a wood-destroying insect inspection on every purchase and include treatment and damaged framing repair in the scope when activity is found.

commonIssues.title: Hidden storm and moisture damage
commonIssues.body: Houses that took water in Katrina or later storms were not always repaired properly. Investors find mold behind drywall, wet insulation, corroded electrical boxes and subfloors that were dried and covered rather than replaced. Humidity on the coast keeps that damage active. We open suspect areas early in demolition, test moisture levels, and price remediation before finish work, because covering a moisture problem in Gulfport just resets the clock on a future callback.

commonIssues.title: Insurance-driven upgrades
commonIssues.body: On the coast, getting a house insured can drive the renovation scope as much as the inspection does. Older electrical panels, aging roofs, missing opening protection and outdated plumbing can make coverage expensive or hard to place, which hurts resale and refinance alike. Buyers' lenders will not close without coverage. We talk through likely insurability items during the walk-through so the scope covers what carriers care about before you price the cosmetic work, and before you lock in your ARV.

investorMarket:
Investor demand in Gulfport has several anchors. The Naval Construction Battalion Center, home of the Seabees, sits in the middle of the city, and Keesler Air Force Base is next door in Biloxi, so military families create steady rental demand for well-kept houses within an easy commute. The Port of Gulfport, the casino and hospitality economy along U.S. 90, and coastal healthcare employers add to it. That makes single-family rentals and BRRRR common strategies, particularly in the post-war neighborhoods between the tracks and I-10 and in the newer subdivisions of Orange Grove.

Flips work best where buyers have financing and insurance options: North Gulfport, Orange Grove and houses already built or raised to current flood requirements closer to the beach. Older raised cottages in Handsboro and Downtown Gulfport appeal to buyers who want coastal character, but the flood and termite questions need clear answers before listing.

The biggest variable in any Gulfport deal is carrying cost after the rehab. Windstorm and flood coverage on the coast can be expensive, which affects both your hold and your buyer's monthly payment. Strong deals here are usually ones where the renovation itself improves insurability: a new roof, updated electrical, opening protection and a documented elevation. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review flags those items so you can weigh them against your exit before you commit.
permits:
Inside city limits, the City of Gulfport's building department handles building, electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits and inspections, and its floodplain management staff review work on properties in special flood hazard areas. Expect permits for structural repairs, roofing, window and door replacements, electrical and plumbing work, HVAC changes and additions. Unincorporated areas such as Lyman and Saucier go through Harrison County instead.

Flood review is the part out-of-town investors underestimate. For houses below base flood elevation, the city will look at the cost of the renovation compared with the structure's value, and a project that crosses the substantial improvement threshold triggers full compliance with current flood rules. Keep receipts and estimates organized, because they may be reviewed.

After Katrina, the coastal counties and their cities moved to modern international building codes with wind and flood provisions, so roofing, window and structural work is inspected with hurricane resistance in mind. Mississippi also requires residential remodeling contractors to be licensed through the Mississippi State Board of Contractors above a set contract value. Genstone coordinates licensed trades, pulls permits, schedules inspections and collects lien waivers with each draw.
climate:
Gulfport has a humid subtropical climate shaped by the Gulf. Hurricane season runs from early summer through fall, and a named storm in the area can shut down crews, delay inspections and tie up roofers for months afterward. Projects with open roofs or missing windows during the peak of the season carry real risk, so we sequence dry-in work early and keep materials secured.

Summer heat and humidity are constant, which means mold grows quickly in any closed, unconditioned house and materials like drywall mud, paint and wood flooring need climate control to install properly. Afternoon thunderstorms are routine, and heavy rain can pond on low lots in Turkey Creek and other low-lying areas. Winters are mild, though occasional freezes reach the coast. Coastal salt air also shortens the life of exterior metal, fasteners and HVAC condensers, so we specify corrosion-resistant hardware on exterior work.

faqs.q: Will my Gulfport renovation trigger flood elevation requirements?
faqs.a: It can. If the house is in a special flood hazard area and sits below base flood elevation, the city compares your renovation cost to the value of the structure. Crossing the substantial improvement threshold means the house must meet current flood rules, which may require raising it. We review the flood zone and elevation certificate during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review so you know which side of that line your scope falls on before you buy.

faqs.q: Do you work in Biloxi, Long Beach and the rest of the coast?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone coordinates vetted, licensed local contractors across the Mississippi Gulf Coast, including Biloxi, Long Beach, Pass Christian, D'Iberville, Ocean Springs and unincorporated Harrison County. Each city has its own building department and floodplain review, and your field manager handles permits and inspections in whichever jurisdiction the property sits in. Flood zones and older housing patterns differ from town to town along U.S. 90, so the scope is written for the specific lot rather than the coast in general.

faqs.q: How do hurricanes affect a renovation schedule in Gulfport?
faqs.a: During hurricane season, we prioritize getting the house dried in: roof, windows, doors and exterior openings before interior finishes. If a storm threatens, crews secure materials and the site. After a major storm, demand for roofers and other trades spikes along the coast, which can slow work. Your field manager keeps you updated and adjusts the schedule as conditions change, with photos showing the state of the house.

faqs.q: Can you help make a Gulfport house easier to insure?
faqs.a: We cannot speak for insurers, but we know which items carriers on the coast commonly ask about: roof age and construction, roof-to-wall connections, opening protection, electrical panel type, and plumbing material. We can include those upgrades in your scope and provide documentation of the work. Talk with your insurance agent early, and we will price the items they identify so the scope supports coverage.

fix-flip.title: Fix and Flip Contractor in Gulfport, MS | Genstone
fix-flip.metaDescription: Gulfport, MS fix and flip renovations scoped around flood zones, wind-rated roofs and insurability so coastal buyers can finance and close on your house.
fix-flip.h1: Fix and Flip Renovations in Gulfport
fix-flip.intro: Selling a renovated house on the Mississippi coast means selling it to a buyer who has to insure it. In Gulfport, a pretty kitchen does not help if the buyer's agent comes back with a windstorm quote that breaks their budget or a lender that wants an elevation certificate you do not have. Genstone scopes Gulfport flips with that buyer in mind. During the free Pre-Offer Rehab Review we check the flood zone, roof, electrical, termite history and past storm repairs alongside your comps and ARV. Then we write a scope that improves the house where coastal buyers and their insurers look first, with labor, materials and a draw schedule. A designated field manager coordinates licensed local trades, handles city permits and floodplain review, and keeps the project moving.

sections.h2: The substantial improvement line decides your budget
sections.body:
For any Gulfport flip in a special flood hazard area, the first number to know is how much you can spend before the city treats the project as a substantial improvement. Cross that line on a house below base flood elevation, and the renovation must bring the whole structure into compliance with current flood rules, which can mean raising it or major changes to the lower level. On a cottage south of the railroad tracks or a low-lying ranch near Turkey Creek, that can change a flip from profitable to unworkable.

We pull the flood zone and any existing elevation certificate early, estimate the structure value the city is likely to use, and write a scope that either stays below the threshold or plans the compliance work openly so it is priced into your offer. Our cost records are organized for the city's review. What we will not do is help split or disguise work to avoid the rule, because it creates problems at resale and with insurers.

sections.h2: Spend where coastal buyers look first
sections.body:
Gulfport buyers, and the agents who show them houses, tend to ask about the roof, the flood zone and the insurance quote before they ask about countertops. A flip with a new roof installed to current wind requirements, updated electrical, a newer HVAC condenser that has not been eaten by salt air, and documentation of termite treatment answers those questions before they become objections.

On the interior, durable and moisture-tolerant finishes make sense here: luxury vinyl plank or tile flooring, solid-surface or quartz counters, and paint suited to humid rooms. In Orange Grove and North Gulfport, buyers compare your house with newer subdivision homes, so clean, functional kitchens and baths carry the sale. In Downtown Gulfport and Handsboro, character features such as original wood floors, porches and tall ceilings are worth preserving when the structure allows. Military buyers connected to the Seabee base or Keesler often buy on a schedule, and a move-in-ready house with clear inspection and insurance answers appeals to them strongly.

sections.h2: Timing a flip around hurricane season
sections.body:
A Gulfport flip that is still open to the weather in late summer is carrying risk you do not need. When a project starts near or during hurricane season, we front-load dry-in work: roof, windows, exterior doors and any siding or sheathing repairs come before interior finishes. Materials are stored securely, and if a storm threatens, crews secure the site.

Scheduling matters on the sales side too. Buyer activity and insurance availability can tighten when a storm is in the Gulf, and after a significant hit, contractors across the coast get booked up for repair work. Listing ahead of the busiest part of the season, or making sure the house is weather-tight if work continues through it, keeps your carrying costs predictable. Your field manager tracks the schedule and long-lead items, and you follow progress through photos and milestone updates, with draws paid only against completed work. If a storm does pass through mid-project, the field manager documents the house afterward so you know exactly where things stand before the next draw.

faqs.q: What makes a Gulfport flip harder to sell?
faqs.a: Insurance and flood questions are the most common obstacles. An old roof, outdated electrical, missing documentation of elevation, or signs of past water or termite damage can make coverage expensive or hard to get, and buyers' lenders require it. Addressing those items in the renovation and providing documentation helps buyers move forward. Finishes matter, but on the coast they usually come second to these basics.

faqs.q: Should I buy a flip south of the railroad tracks in Gulfport?
faqs.a: It can work, but the flood rules require careful planning. Many houses closer to the beach are in high-risk flood zones, so the substantial improvement threshold limits what you can spend without bringing the house into full compliance. Houses that were already rebuilt or raised after Katrina can be easier. We review the flood zone and elevation certificate before you commit so the numbers reflect the real scope.

faqs.q: Which finishes hold up best in a Gulfport flip?
faqs.a: Moisture-tolerant materials do well: luxury vinyl plank or tile floors, quartz or solid-surface counters, moisture-resistant drywall in baths, and quality exterior paint. Outside, corrosion-resistant fasteners and hardware last longer in salt air. In older raised cottages, refinishing original wood floors can be a selling point if the subfloor and framing are sound and free of termite damage. Avoid carpet in most rooms, since it holds moisture in a humid coastal house.

brrrr.title: BRRRR Rehab Contractor in Gulfport, MS | Genstone
brrrr.metaDescription: BRRRR rehab in Gulfport, MS: renovations that support the refinance appraisal, improve coastal insurability and stand up to military and workforce tenants.
brrrr.intro: BRRRR on the Mississippi coast has one extra moving part most inland investors never think about: the insurance premium that lands on your DSCR calculation after the refinance. In Gulfport, a house that appraises well can still struggle to cash flow if the windstorm and flood coverage is expensive. Genstone writes BRRRR scopes that serve the appraisal and the long hold at once. We focus on improvements appraisers credit, upgrades that tend to make houses easier to insure, and materials that stand up to tenants and humid coastal conditions. The free Pre-Offer Rehab Review checks repair costs, flood zone, roof condition and ARV before you commit. A designated field manager then coordinates licensed local trades and city permits, and Genstone Financial offers DSCR rental loans if you want the refinance handled alongside the rehab.

sections.h2: Why insurance belongs in the BRRRR math in Gulfport
sections.body:
In most markets, the refinance question is simply whether the appraisal supports the loan. In Gulfport, the lender will also look at the property's debt service coverage, and coastal windstorm and flood premiums are part of that expense line. A house with an old roof, no opening protection and outdated electrical may carry a premium that makes the DSCR ratio tight even at a good rent.

That is why our Gulfport BRRRR scopes often prioritize a new roof built to current wind requirements, proper roof-to-wall connections where they are missing, updated electrical panels and plumbing, and well-documented work. Houses north of I-10 in Orange Grove and North Gulfport often sit in lower-risk flood zones, which can make the numbers easier. Closer to the beach, an elevation certificate showing the house sits at or above base flood elevation can make a real difference in the flood premium. We help you gather and organize that documentation so both your insurer and your lender have a clear picture at refinance time.

Gulfport appraisals lean on nearby sales, and the comp pool can vary sharply between post-Katrina rebuilds, older unrenovated houses and newer subdivisions. A renovated 1960s ranch between the tracks and the interstate may need to be compared with houses that were gutted and rebuilt after the storm, which means your renovation has to bring it up to that standard to compete.

Appraisers credit what they can verify: updated kitchens and baths, new roofs and HVAC, sound flooring, and a structure that shows no active termite or moisture damage. Because Formosan termites are common on the coast, we recommend treatment and documentation as part of the scope; an appraiser who notes damage or activity can create problems for the lender. A completed-work summary with photos, permits and inspection results gives the appraiser a clear record. It does not guide the number, but it helps the appraiser place your house with renovated comps instead of with the as-is stock nearby.

sections.h2: Built for military and workforce tenants
sections.body:
A large part of Gulfport's rental demand comes from military households tied to the Naval Construction Battalion Center and Keesler Air Force Base, along with port, hospitality and healthcare workers. Military tenants often relocate on orders, which means regular turnover, and they tend to expect a clean, functional, well-maintained house. A durable renovation keeps those turns short and inexpensive.

We specify water-resistant flooring throughout, washable wall finishes, solid cabinet boxes, quality fixtures that are easy to service, and HVAC sized for the coastal summer with condensers protected from salt air where possible. Exterior work uses corrosion-resistant fasteners and materials that handle humidity. Gutters and grading keep water away from the foundation and out of the crawlspace on raised houses. Each choice is aimed at the same outcome: fewer maintenance calls and faster turnovers between military families on the move. Our one-year workmanship warranty covers the renovation itself; tenant damage and normal wear fall outside it.

faqs.q: Does flood insurance affect a Gulfport BRRRR refinance?
faqs.a: Often, yes. A DSCR lender looks at your expenses, including insurance, against the rent. In higher-risk flood zones, flood and windstorm premiums can be significant. Upgrades like a new roof built to current wind requirements and documentation such as an elevation certificate can help your insurance quote. We price those items in the scope so you can test the refinance before you buy.

faqs.q: Which Gulfport areas work best for BRRRR?
faqs.a: Post-war neighborhoods between the railroad tracks and I-10, plus subdivisions in Orange Grove and North Gulfport, are common targets because they draw steady rental demand from military and workforce tenants and often sit in lower-risk flood zones. The best deals combine a reasonable purchase price, supportive comps and manageable insurance. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review helps you test all three before committing.

faqs.q: Can Genstone handle the refinance and property management too?
faqs.a: Genstone Financial offers DSCR rental loans, and Genstone Property Management can lease and manage the house after the rehab. Both are optional. If you use your own lender or manager, we still provide the scope, draw records and completion documentation they need. Your field manager focuses on finishing the Gulfport renovation so the house is ready for appraisal and tenants.

rental-renovation.title: Rental Property Renovation in Gulfport, MS | Genstone
rental-renovation.metaDescription: Gulfport, MS single-family rental renovations built for salt air, humidity and military turnover, with termite, roof and moisture work handled first.
rental-renovation.intro: A Gulfport rental portfolio lives in a harsh environment. Salt air works on condensers and exterior metal, humidity feeds mold in any house left closed, Formosan termites look for wet wood, and every hurricane season brings a fresh round of roof checks. Add frequent turnover from military households on orders and you have a portfolio that rewards durable, repeatable renovations. Genstone renovates and turns single-family rentals for individual landlords, funds and institutional owners in Gulfport and across Harrison County. We write scopes to a consistent portfolio standard, coordinate vetted, licensed local contractors, and handle city permits and inspections. A designated field manager documents every house with photos and completion records, and Genstone Field Services can cover inspections, occupied maintenance and turn and make-ready work between full renovations.

sections.h2: A rental spec for coastal conditions
sections.body:
The materials that last in an inland rental do not always last in Gulfport. Our coastal rental standard starts outside: corrosion-resistant fasteners and hardware, exterior paint and caulk rated for high humidity, gutters that move water well away from the house, and roofs maintained or replaced with storm season in mind. HVAC condensers get placed and protected thoughtfully, because salt air shortens their life.

Inside, we standardize on waterproof flooring, moisture-resistant drywall in baths, exhaust fans that actually vent outside, and dehumidification where a house struggles to stay dry. Raised cottages get crawlspace attention, with vapor barriers and checks for wet framing that would draw termites. Fixtures and finishes are kept consistent across your houses so maintenance techs carry the same parts and repairs go quickly. The point of the standard is not to make every house identical. It is to keep each one from failing in the same predictable ways coastal houses usually fail.

sections.h2: Termites, moisture and the annual check
sections.body:
Formosan termites are one of the most expensive surprises in a Gulfport rental, because colonies can grow large and damage framing before anyone notices. They are attracted to moisture, which means a slow plumbing leak or a roof drip can create a new nesting point well above ground. A rental program here should include regular termite inspections, a treatment plan with documentation, and fast repair of any leak a tenant reports.

We fold that into our rental work. Every renovation and every turn includes a look at the usual trouble spots: under sinks, around tubs and water heaters, at window sills, along the roofline and in the crawlspace on raised houses. When we find soft wood, mud tubes or swarmers, we document it, coordinate treatment and price the structural repair. Catching it at a turn costs far less than replacing framing after a tenant reports a sagging floor, and it keeps the house insurable and easier to sell later.

Military tenants tied to the Seabee base and Keesler move on orders, and they often move during busy relocation periods. That creates turnovers in clusters, and a portfolio owner who cannot turn houses quickly loses rent while the next family rents elsewhere. Genstone runs Gulfport turns as a repeatable process.

After move-out, a field inspection documents condition with photos and builds a scope against your standard, separating tenant damage from normal wear so deposit decisions are clear. Trades are sequenced so paint follows drywall repair and flooring goes in after plumbing checks. Where a turn falls during hurricane season, we look at the roof and exterior openings while we are on site. You approve the scope, follow progress remotely and pay against completed work. The aim is a clean, safe house ready for the next tenant, with records that help if questions come up during the following lease. Over time, those records also show which houses cost the most to turn, which is useful when deciding what to hold and what to sell.

faqs.q: Do you manage rental turns in Gulfport as well as renovations?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone handles full renovations and recurring turns, and Genstone Field Services can cover make-ready work, inspections and occupied maintenance between larger projects. Each turn starts with a documented inspection and a scope written to your portfolio standard. You approve the work, track it through photos and pay against completed work. Because many Gulfport turns follow military relocations, we plan for clusters of move-outs and keep crews lined up ahead of time.

faqs.q: How do you handle termites in Gulfport rentals?
faqs.a: We look for termite activity and moisture problems at every renovation and turn, especially around plumbing, windows, rooflines and crawlspaces. When we find activity or damage, we document it, coordinate treatment with a licensed pest control company and price the structural repair. Formosan termites are common on the Gulf Coast, so regular inspections and fast leak repair are worth building into your rental program.

faqs.q: Can you renovate rentals across Harrison County?
faqs.a: Yes. We coordinate vetted, licensed local contractors in Gulfport, Biloxi, Long Beach, D'Iberville, Pass Christian and unincorporated Harrison County, and handle permits and floodplain review in each jurisdiction. A single portfolio standard keeps materials consistent, and your field manager documents every property so you can manage the group remotely. Houses in different flood zones may need different exterior details, and the scope notes those differences property by property.

multifamily-renovation.title: Duplex & 2–4 Unit Renovation in Gulfport, MS | Genstone
multifamily-renovation.metaDescription: Gulfport, MS duplex and fourplex renovations: phased work around tenants, shared roofs and systems rebuilt for wind and flood rules, permits handled.
multifamily-renovation.h1: Duplex and Small Multifamily Renovation in Gulfport
multifamily-renovation.intro: Small multifamily on the Mississippi coast comes in a few distinct forms. There are older frame duplexes and houses converted to apartments in Downtown Gulfport and nearby neighborhoods, brick duplexes and fourplexes from the 1960s through the 1980s along the commercial corridors, and post-Katrina rebuilds where owners replaced a lost house with two units. Each one shares a roof, a foundation and usually a sewer line, which in Gulfport means shared exposure to wind, flood and termites. Genstone renovates 2–4 unit buildings for investors who want higher rents, lower operating costs and buildings that are easier to insure. We coordinate vetted, licensed local trades, plan work around occupied units, and handle city permits and floodplain review. A designated field manager keeps you informed from the first walk-through through final billing.

sections.h2: One roof, several tenants, coastal exposure
sections.body:
In a Gulfport duplex or fourplex, the roof is the single most important shared component. One leak can damage several units at once, and on the coast, an older roof is also what drives windstorm premiums up. Replacing it to current wind requirements, with proper connections to the walls and sealed decking, is often the first investment that makes sense in a small multifamily building here.

Flood exposure works the same way. If the building sits in a special flood hazard area and below base flood elevation, the substantial improvement threshold applies to the whole structure, not each unit, so a combined renovation across all units can cross it faster than investors expect. We review the flood zone and any elevation certificate during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review and plan the scope accordingly. Shared sewer lines, older electrical services and termite damage in shared framing round out the list of items we price on separate lines before finishes are discussed.

sections.h2: Phasing work in occupied Gulfport buildings
sections.body:
Most small multifamily purchases in Gulfport come with tenants, and many of those tenants work at the port, the base, casinos or local hospitals on shifting schedules. That affects how work is phased. Vacant units get the full interior renovation first. Occupied units are done at lease turnover or through agreed access windows, with notice given well ahead.

Exterior and shared work, like the roof, siding, gutters, drainage and exterior paint, can go on without entering units, which is a good reason to plan it early, especially before hurricane season. Utility work on shared systems, such as a main drain replacement or a service upgrade, is scheduled with short, announced shutoffs. Air conditioning is not optional in a Gulf Coast summer, so HVAC replacements in occupied units are scheduled carefully and finished the same day whenever possible. Lead-safe practices apply in pre-1978 buildings, with containment that protects the families living on the other side of the wall.

Duplexes built after 2005 to replace houses lost in Katrina were generally built under modern wind and flood codes, which makes them easier to renovate and insure. Their scopes tend to focus on interior wear, aging builder-grade fixtures and HVAC, and checking that original construction details like flashing and drainage have held up.

Older buildings and converted houses are a different job. Expect patched roofs, older electrical with shared or undersized services, cast-iron or clay sewer lines, termite damage in sills and framing, and fire separation between units that may not meet current expectations. Before planning finishes, we confirm the legal unit count with the city and price the work to add smoke and carbon monoxide detection, improve separation, separate utilities where practical, and repair structural damage. Listing each of those as its own line lets you compare the cost against the rent increase and decide what to do now and what can wait until the next turnover.

faqs.q: Does the flood substantial improvement rule apply to a whole duplex?
faqs.a: Yes. The threshold is based on the value of the entire structure and the cost of the work on it, so renovating several units in one project counts together. On a Gulfport duplex below base flood elevation, that can trigger full flood compliance faster than renovating a single-family house. We check the flood zone and elevation during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review and plan the scope around it.

faqs.q: Can tenants stay in place during a Gulfport multifamily renovation?
faqs.a: Usually. We complete vacant units first and handle occupied units at turnover or during scheduled access windows. Exterior and shared-system work is planned with notice and short shutoffs, and HVAC replacements are finished quickly because cooling is essential on the coast. Your field manager coordinates schedules with you or your property manager, and tenants working shifts at the port, base or casinos get access windows that fit their hours.

faqs.q: What should I inspect before buying a small multifamily in Gulfport?
faqs.a: Look at the roof age and construction, flood zone and elevation certificate, termite history and current activity, the sewer line, the electrical service, and fire separation between units. Confirm the legal unit count with the city. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review checks those items and estimates the repairs so you can compare them against your expected rents before you make an offer.

fha-203k.title: FHA 203(k) Contractor in Gulfport, MS | Genstone
fha-203k.metaDescription: FHA 203(k) certified contractor serving Gulfport, MS buyers, agents and lenders: coastal roof, termite and flood-aware bids that work with draw inspections.
fha-203k.intro: Gulfport has plenty of houses that a first-time buyer could afford and would love to live in, but that need work before an FHA appraiser or insurer will accept them: an aging roof, termite damage, old electrical, a dated bath. An FHA 203(k) loan lets the buyer finance both the purchase and the repairs. Genstone Construction is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor, and we work with buyers, agents, loan officers and 203(k) consultants to produce bids that fit coastal conditions and the program's rules. We also flag early when a house's flood zone or elevation could complicate the renovation. After closing, a designated field manager coordinates vetted, licensed local trades, handles city permits and floodplain review, and organizes documentation for each draw inspection.

sections.h2: Limited or Standard on the coast
sections.body:
The Limited 203(k) is meant for non-structural work and is capped at $75,000. On the Gulf Coast, that is often enough for a buyer who needs a new roof, HVAC, electrical and plumbing updates, flooring, and kitchen or bath work in a structurally sound house. Many post-war ranches between the tracks and I-10 and houses in Orange Grove fit this profile.

The Standard 203(k) is needed for structural repairs, including major termite damage to framing, foundation or pier work on raised houses, additions, or extensive remodeling, and it requires a HUD-approved 203(k) consultant. Repairs must total at least $5,000 to qualify. One Gulfport-specific factor applies to both: if the house sits below base flood elevation in a special flood hazard area, the scope must stay within flood rules, and crossing the substantial improvement threshold could require raising the house. We check that before the buyer goes under contract so the loan type and scope are realistic from the start.

sections.h2: Gulfport houses that make good 203(k) candidates
sections.body:
The best 203(k) houses in Gulfport tend to be solid structures with clear, fixable problems. A 1960s brick ranch north of the tracks with an old roof, original electrical and a worn kitchen is a classic example. So is a newer house in Orange Grove or North Gulfport that suffered from deferred maintenance and needs HVAC, flooring and paint. Older raised cottages in Downtown Gulfport or Soria City can also work for buyers who want character, but they usually need a Standard 203(k) because termite and pier repairs are structural.

Harder cases include houses with unresolved storm damage, extensive mold, or uncertain flood compliance, especially closer to the beach. These are not always impossible, but they need careful evaluation by the consultant and contractor before the buyer commits. Lead-based paint rules apply to houses built before 1978, which covers a large share of the older Gulfport stock and affects how painted surfaces are handled in the scope.

sections.h2: How our 203(k) bids and draws work
sections.body:
Lenders and consultants need bids that are detailed enough to underwrite and verify. Ours break out labor and materials by trade, describe the work clearly, and include a draw schedule matched to completed stages. On Standard loans, we coordinate with the consultant so the bid matches the work write-up before submission. If the flood or insurance review requires specific items, such as roof upgrades for a windstorm policy, we include them so the buyer can close.

After closing, work proceeds in stages. Each draw request comes with photos and completion documentation, and the consultant or lender inspection confirms the work before funds are released. Your field manager handles city permits and inspections so approvals line up with draws. During hurricane season, we prioritize dry-in work to protect the house and the buyer's investment. There is no upfront payment from the buyer, and the final payment follows completion and approval. Agents get regular updates so they can keep their buyer informed without chasing the contractor for answers.

faqs.q: Can a 203(k) loan pay for a new roof in Gulfport?
faqs.a: Yes. Roof replacement is a common 203(k) repair, and it is usually eligible under the Limited 203(k) if no structural framing work is required. On the coast, replacing an older roof to current wind requirements also tends to help with insurance, which the buyer needs to close. We include roof details in the bid so the lender and insurer can see what is being done.

faqs.q: Does a flood zone affect a 203(k) renovation in Gulfport?
faqs.a: It can. If the house is in a special flood hazard area and below base flood elevation, the renovation must follow local flood rules, and a project crossing the substantial improvement threshold may require raising the house. We check flood zone and elevation information before the buyer commits, so the loan type and scope are realistic. Houses north of I-10 often avoid this issue entirely, while older homes nearer the beach usually need a closer look.

faqs.q: Is Genstone certified for FHA 203(k) work?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone holds the FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor designation and takes on coastal Mississippi projects, where we prepare bids for lenders and consultants, coordinate vetted, licensed local trades on the Gulf Coast, and document each draw. Final approval of the loan and contractor rests with the lender, so talk to your loan officer early and bring us in when you have a target house. We can usually tell the buyer during the first walk-through whether the Limited or Standard version fits.

reo-renovation.title: REO & Bank-Owned Renovation in Gulfport, MS | Genstone
reo-renovation.metaDescription: REO renovation in Gulfport, MS for servicers, banks and GSEs: storm-damaged, mold-affected and termite-damaged vacant houses stabilized and documented.
reo-renovation.h1: REO and Bank-Owned Property Renovation in Gulfport
reo-renovation.intro: A vacant house on the Mississippi coast deteriorates faster than one inland. Humidity builds inside within days of the power going off, roof leaks feed mold and Formosan termites, salt air works on anything metal, and a tropical storm can turn a minor problem into a claim. Gulfport REO files also come with flood zone and elevation questions that affect what the asset can be repaired to and who can buy it. Genstone works with mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and Government-Sponsored Enterprises, for which we are a preferred contractor, to secure, stabilize and renovate bank-owned property across Gulfport and Harrison County. Genstone Field Services handles property preservation, inspections and code compliance, and our renovation team prices and completes repairs through vetted, licensed local trades with full documentation for each file.

sections.body:
The first priority on a coastal REO is to stop the damage. That means securing entries and openings, tarping or temporarily repairing any roof leak, drying out wet areas, and getting moisture under control before mold spreads further. Where power is available, running the HVAC or dehumidifiers can make a large difference in a humid Gulfport summer. During hurricane season, we also look at loose exterior items, damaged openings and anything that could become debris or let wind and water in.

Our initial inspection documents the condition of the house with photos and a written report, identifying immediate hazards, active leaks, mold, termite activity, theft of HVAC equipment or copper, and any signs of past storm damage that was not repaired. That record helps the asset manager decide on next steps and supports any insurance claim for damage that occurred during the holding period. Field Services keeps the property maintained, including grass and overgrowth, which code enforcement watches closely on vacant houses.

sections.h2: Flood, storm and termite history on REO files
sections.body:
Many Gulfport REO properties have a complicated history: water from Katrina or a later storm, repairs that may or may not have been permitted, and termite activity that went untreated while the owner was in default. Before recommending a repair scope, we look for evidence of each. That includes moisture readings and opening suspect walls, checking for mud tubes and damaged framing, and noting signs of past repairs that look incomplete.

Flood zone and elevation matter for disposition. If the house sits in a special flood hazard area below base flood elevation, extensive repairs can trigger substantial improvement review, which limits how much can be done without bringing the house into full flood compliance. We flag that early so asset managers can weigh a lighter repair, an as-is sale to investors, or a larger compliance project. When the house is in a lower-risk zone, a fuller renovation for owner-occupant buyers may make more sense.

sections.h2: Repair options and documentation for asset managers
sections.body:
Asset managers need choices, not just a single bid. For Gulfport REO properties, we typically price a few levels of repair: safety, code and weatherproofing items only; a market-ready repair that addresses what buyers' lenders and insurers usually flag, such as roof condition and electrical; and, where the numbers support it, a fuller renovation aimed at owner-occupant buyers. Each option includes labor, materials, debris removal and dumpsters, and is organized by priority.

Work is documented throughout with before, during and after photos, completion records, lien waivers and contractor compliance paperwork. Draws are tied to completed work. If a buyer's inspection on a listed property finds something new, the same field manager can price and complete the repair without starting the vendor process over. That continuity helps servicers, GSE programs and institutional owners keep files clean and move Gulfport properties to closing. Because roofs and insurance drive so many coastal buyer objections, we also note the roof's age and condition clearly in every repair option so brokers can answer those questions upfront.

faqs.q: What should a servicer expect when inspecting a vacant Gulfport REO?
faqs.a: Expect moisture and mold issues, especially if the power was off through warm months, along with possible termite damage, roof leaks, theft of HVAC units or copper, and signs of past storm damage. Our first inspection documents each issue with photos and separates emergency items from the full repair list so the asset manager can approve urgent work quickly. Humidity damage accelerates on the coast, so speed on that first approval matters.

faqs.q: Can Genstone handle hurricane preparation on REO properties?
faqs.a: We can secure loose exterior items, check and repair openings, tarp or temporarily repair roofs and document the property's condition before a storm. After a storm, we inspect, document damage for claims and stabilize the property. Field Services also handles ongoing preservation tasks on vacant Gulfport houses between storms, including lawn care, debris removal and regular condition checks, so problems are found before the next storm season arrives.

faqs.q: Do flood rules limit repairs on bank-owned houses in Gulfport?
faqs.a: They can. If the house is below base flood elevation in a special flood hazard area, extensive repairs can trigger the substantial improvement requirement. We review flood zone and elevation information before recommending a scope so asset managers can choose between lighter repairs, an as-is sale or a larger compliance project. Properties north of I-10 are less likely to face this limit than those near the beach, but every file is checked.
